texts.preamble: Parag Audholia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 April, 2024 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain Criminal Revision No. 1352 Of 2024. Between :- 1. Parag Audholia S/O Shri B.K. Audholia, Aged About 54 Years, Occupation: Business Resident Of 913 Wright Town Jabalpur District Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh). 2. Surjeet Nandi S/O Late Shri Shiv Prasad Nandi, Aged About 56 Years, Occupation: The Then Manager Prestige Princess R/O House No. 83, Mohrab Colony Adarsh Nagar Jabalpur District Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) ....Petitioners (By Shri Manish Datt- Senior Advocate With Shri Satyam Rai - Advocate. ) And The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Food Inspector Amrish Dubey Deputy Director Food And Drug Administration Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) . ....Respondent (By Shri Akhilendra Singh - Government Advocate) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Reserved on : 20/03/2024 Pronounced on : 05/04/2024 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2 Parag Audholia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58243131/ 1
texts.facts: The present revision has been filed challenging the order dated 07.03.2024 passed by the learned appellate Court whereby the application filed by the present petitioners under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. for adducing additional evidence has been rejected. 2. The brief facts leading to the present controversy as advanced by learned senior counsel for the petitioners are that the present petitioners were prosecuted for offencse under Section 7(ii) /16 (1)(a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 (for short hereinafter referred to as Act of 1954). The present petitioners have been convicted for the aforesaid offence with sentence of one year R.I. and fine. During pendency of the said appeal the present petitioners filed an application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. to summon one Sanjay Arora who is proprietor of "Sugar Dealer" which is a firm from which the questioned commodity is said to be purchased by the petitioners.
texts.arguments: 3. The substratum of the prosecution case against the present petitioners is that the present petitioners are the Manager and Proprietor of one restaurant establishment namely "Hotel Prestige Princess" and on 17.06.2011 there was a inspection in the said hotel by the concerned authority and during the course of inspection, it was found that some packets of Chinese Noodles were kept in the restaurant and team purchased three packets of noodles on payment of price of the said packets and obtained receipt. When the said noodles were subjected to examination in the laboratory, then though no harmful or injurious adulterants were found in the packets of noodles but the packets were found to be mis-branded. 4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that as per Section 19 of the Act of 1954, it is provided in sub-section (2) that the vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to sale of any adulterated or mis-branded food articles article of food if he proves that he purchased the article of food from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warranty in the prescribed form. It is further argued that as per proviso to Section 14, the bill, cash memorandum or invoice issued by a vendor of the article shall be deemed to be a warranty given by such manufacturer, distributor or dealer under this section. Thus, it is argued that the present petitioners had purchased the packets of noodles from "Sugar Dealer" firm and the deposition of proprietor of that firm is necessary to prove warranty. It is further argued that in terms of Section 20 (A) of Act 1954 the Court can proceed suo-motu against the manufacturer, distributor or dealer of any article of food. Thus, Parag Audholia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58243131/ 2 it is contended that even if petitioners had not requested for summoning the proprietor of such firm, even than the trial court as well as appellate court were duty bound to implead the said person as accused. Thus, it is contended that to prove the innocence of present petitioners, the deposition of Sanjay Arora, proprietor of "Sugar Dealer" is essential. It is further contended by learned senior counsel that the sole consideration of application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. at appellate stage should be to meet the ends of justice and mere filing of application at belated stage is not a sufficient ground to reject the application. The judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Brigadier Sukhjeet Singh (Retired) MVC Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others 2019 (16) SCC 712 is relied. 5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the revision and has contended that the petitioners have filed the application belatedly and petitioners were given full opportunity to prove their innocence during the course of the trial and now to fill up the lacuna they cannot be allowed to misuse and abuse the provision of Section 391 of Cr.P.C. 6. 7. In the present case the contention of petitioners is that they need to prove the bill so as to substantiate the defence in terms of Section 14 of Act of 1954 on the ground that they had purchased the food articles under warranty from the dealer. They want to proprietor of that "Sugar Dealer" firm to prove that the food articles were in fact purchased under the bill from that vendor. 12. So far as the reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Brigadier Sukhjeet Singh (Retired) MVC Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others 2019 (16) SCC 712 is concerned, the said case turns on different factual back ground. In these circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the certified copy of trust deed can be taken on record by appellate Court by exercising jurisdiction of u/s 391 Cr.P.C. to meet ends of justice. 14. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Zahira Habibullah Sheikh & Anr vs State Of Gujarat & Ors 2004(4) SCC 158 has held that Section 391 of the Code is another salutary provision which clothes the courts with the power to effectively decide an appeal. Though Section 386 envisages the normal and ordinary manner and method of disposal of an appeal, yet it does not and cannot be said to exhaustively enumerate the modes by which alone the court can deal with an appeal. 15. In a recent judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ajitsinh Chehuji Rathod Vs. State of Gujarat and Another 2024 SCC OnLine SC 77 has held as under:- Parag Audholia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58243131/ 4 "17.
